title: Swinburne Student HQ conversation
body: VTAC process, fashion course, English requirement, fees. [Notes](https://github.com/tkluysk/higher-ed-explorer/blob/main/transcripts/2026-09-28-swinburne-student-hq.md)

title: UniMelb Prospective Students meeting
body: NCEA→ATAR change, maths prerequisite, fees, housing timing. [Notes](https://github.com/tkluysk/higher-ed-explorer/blob/main/transcripts/2026-10-02-unimelb-prospective-students.md)

title: Reply to the Swinburne adviser's summary email
body: From her own email account: once she's an applicant, Swinburne will only correspond with her. Ask about fashion materials, placement partners and a (virtual) session with the fashion academics.

title: Decide on Calculus and Probability Online
body: UniMelb's online maths bridging subject, covering similar ground to VCE Mathematical Methods 3/4. A pass (50%+) meets the maths prerequisite for Biomedicine, Science, Commerce and Agriculture. That's a formal box ticked, not a reason to drop maths in Year 13: first-year science everywhere assumes it, and Otago strongly recommends Level 3 Calculus. It gives no credit towards a degree. It assumes VCE Methods 1/2 (roughly NCEA Level 2 Maths: algebra, functions and graphs, intro calculus). Two modules: **Calculus** (functions, limits, differentiation, integration; A$660) and **Probability** (sets, counting, conditional probability, tree diagrams; A$330), A$990 for both. Summer workload: 23–30 hours a week for both modules. Which module(s) count depends on prior study, and UniMelb recommends both if unsure, so email the NCEA maths record to online-calcprob@unimelb.edu.au and ask before registering. Summer results can't be used for entry that same year (2027), but they're in time for a 2028 start. Working plan: the Calculus module only, with probability covered by Level 2 Probability and Level 3 Statistics in Year 13, if UniMelb agrees (asked by email). UniMelb is the strict one. Sydney's medical science degrees (USyd, UNSW, UTS, Macquarie, Western Sydney) list maths only as assumed knowledge. NZ biomedical degrees (Otago, Auckland, Victoria, Canterbury) need only University Entrance, though Otago strongly recommends Level 3 Calculus. Monash keeps its own list of alternatives. RMIT and Swinburne fashion have no maths prerequisite. [Course page](https://ms.unimelb.edu.au/study/online-calculus-and-probability) · [Overview video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MAHRUXG1gMI) · [Monash maths prerequisites](https://www.monash.edu/study/courses/entry-requirements/math-science-prerequisite/)

title: Take UniMelb's Test Yourself quiz
body: After the Level 2 maths external. Do it timed and closed-book, then mark it against the Mathematical Methods 1 and 2 summary: tick each topic as confident, shaky or never seen. The gaps decide the December revision and help answer which module(s) to take. [Methods 1 & 2 summary](https://ms.unimelb.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0020/3501272/MM_1and2_Summary.pdf) · [Test Yourself quiz](https://ms.unimelb.edu.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0018/3501261/CalculusAndProbability-TestYourselfQuiz.pdf)

title: Calculus and Probability: Summer 2027 registration opens
body: Opens 10 am Melbourne, which is **12 noon NZ** (1 pm if the page's "AEST" is meant literally). Closes 11:59 pm Melbourne on Mon 4 Jan, which is 1:59 am NZ on Tue 5 Jan, the day after the course starts. Register early: withdrawing before the start refunds all but 10%. [Course page](https://ms.unimelb.edu.au/study/online-calculus-and-probability)

title: December revision block for Calculus and Probability
body: About 4–5 hours a week until Christmas, on the gaps the quiz found. Likely gaps beyond NCEA Level 2: logarithms and exponential functions, graphs and transformations of functions, polynomials (factor theorem, cubics), circular functions in radians, counting (permutations and combinations), and differentiation from first principles. Redo the quiz in the first week of January.

title: Calculus and Probability summer intensive starts
body: 6 teaching weeks, to Fri 12 Feb. Each week: watch the lecture videos, submit the weekly questions and join the online Zoom consultations (needs a webcam). UniMelb's estimate for Summer is **23–30 hours a week for both modules**, 16–20 for Calculus only and 7–10 for Probability only. That's close to a full-time job for 6 weeks; the overview video's 8–12 hours is for the longer offerings. Each week's material is released at the start of that week, so work can't be done ahead. Needs a computer and reliable internet every week, so plan summer trips around it. Tutorial times are in Melbourne time; add 2 hours for NZ (both are on daylight saving until 4 Apr). [Overview video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MAHRUXG1gMI)

title: Last refund point for Calculus and Probability (end of week 2)
body: Withdrawing by the end of week 2 refunds all but 20%; after that, nothing. Use the first two weeks to judge whether the workload fits the summer.

title: Send NCEA Level 2 results to Swinburne for the English check
body: The adviser offered to have admissions check whether her English meets the bachelor's prerequisite. Expected answer: take English in Year 13 anyway.

title: Year 13 starts — keep English and Chemistry
body: English for the English prerequisite (Swinburne, UniMelb); Chemistry for UniMelb Biomedicine. Schools start between 28 Jan and 3 Feb. If doing the Calculus and Probability intensive, its last two weeks and the 22 Feb exam fall in the first weeks of term. Level 3 Statistics counts towards the rank score and ATAR, but doesn't meet UniMelb's maths prerequisite; Level 3 Calculus needs Level 2 algebra and calculus. So a failed bridging course is retaken (Autumn or Spring 2027), not covered at school. [MoE term dates](https://www.education.govt.nz/term-dates-and-holidays)

title: Calculus and Probability teaching ends
body: The last two teaching weeks overlap the start of Year 13. SWOT-VAC (revision week) runs 15–21 Feb, so revision happens in the evenings around school.

title: Calculus and Probability exam (online)
body: Monday, sat online via Zoom with an invigilator, in week 4 of NZ Term 1. Writing time is 1.5 hours for one module or 3 hours for both, plus 15 minutes' reading. The start time isn't published yet: add 2 hours for NZ, so a 9 am Melbourne start runs 11:00 to about 14:15 NZ. Tell the school early, as it takes most of a school day. A mark of 50%+ is needed to pass.

title: Calculus and Probability results returned
body: Some results can be prioritised for 24 Feb. **Pass:** the UniMelb maths prerequisite is met, so keep the result for the VTAC application in August. **Fail or withdrawn:** retake in the Semester 1 (9 weeks, Mar–May) or Semester 2 (Aug–Oct) intake, alongside Year 13, or switch to UniLearn Senior Mathematics (self-paced).

title: Shortlist UniMelb residential colleges (est.)
body: Colleges open applications from about March, run their own interviews and are largely full by September. Fees about $31k–$46k a year, catered. [Colleges FAQ](https://www.colleges.unimelb.edu.au/frequently-asked-questions/)

title: UniMelb online info sessions for NZ students (est. Apr–May)
body: Ask: the official NCEA→ATAR wording, whether ATAR guarantees apply to NCEA, scholarships for NZ citizens.

title: Fashion portfolio draft ready
body: Swinburne: 10-page PDF (at least 5 works, process welcome) + 250 words. RMIT: folio + selection task, assessed in order of submission until places fill. [Swinburne portfolio guidelines](https://www.swinburne.edu.au/media/swinburneeduau/study-at-swinburne/docs/pdfs/portfolio_guidelines_UG_design.pdf)

title: Start housing applications
body: UniMelb said to start around July 2027 for a 2028 start. Private residences open bookings about a year ahead. [Accommodation map](https://tkluysk.github.io/higher-ed-explorer/accommodation.html)

title: Swinburne Open Day (est.)
body: Late July, Hawthorn. Fashion studios open and academics available — usually not otherwise. [Open Day](https://www.swinburne.edu.au/openday/)

title: UniMelb University Accommodation applications open (est.)
body: Accommodation Offer for students new to Melbourne: first come, first served. You can apply before a course offer. [How to apply](https://study.unimelb.edu.au/accommodation/how-to-apply)

title: VTAC applications open (est.)
body: One application, up to 8 course preferences (courses, not universities). Required when applying to more than one Victorian provider. [VTAC key dates](https://vtac.edu.au/dates.html)

title: RMIT Open Day — Brunswick & City (est.)
body: Early–mid August. School of Fashion & Textiles at Brunswick.

title: UniMelb Open Day (est.)
body: A Sunday in August, the only time guided tours run and faculty staff are available. [Open Day](https://study.unimelb.edu.au/openday)

title: NZ halls of residence applications open (est.)
body: If Otago Health Sciences First Year or an Auckland health first year is on the list. Halls fill early and take separate applications from the university; Check the 2027 dates for each.

title: VTAC on-time applications close (est.)
body: Late September (28 Sep in 2026). Applying later costs more but is otherwise treated the same, except some equity schemes and arts and music courses. Lodge the RMIT and Swinburne fashion portfolios early too.

title: Residential colleges largely full
body: Per UniMelb's Prospective Students team. Have a college decision (or a University Accommodation application) in by now.

title: VTAC equity schemes & scholarships (SEAS) close (est.)
body: Early October (9 Oct in 2026); no late applications. Covers UniMelb's Access Melbourne.

title: VTAC late applications close (est.)
body: Higher fee; then a very late window to early December.

title: NZ university applications close (est.)
body: Apply directly to each university; there is no central portal. Auckland's limited-entry programmes, including the Bachelor of Biomedical Science, closed 8 Dec 2026 for 2027. Otago (Health Sciences First Year) and Victoria have their own dates. [NZ medical routes](https://tkluysk.github.io/higher-ed-explorer/index.html#pathways)

title: NCEA results and NZQA ATAR released (est.)
body: Mid-January. NZQA computes an ATAR from the best 90 Level 3 credits (max 24 per subject); from 2027 entry UniMelb uses this. [NZQA: Study in Australia](https://www2.nzqa.govt.nz/international/nz-quals-overseas/study-with-ncea/australia/)

title: Change of preference — reorder with results in hand (est.)
VTAC January round 2 offers (est.)
body: With NCEA results arriving mid-January, this is the realistic round (27 Jan in 2027).

title: Accept offer, enrol in units, confirm housing
body: Enrol early: electives fill first-come, first-served. Confirm or cancel the housing booking within its withdrawal terms.

title: First semester fees due — paid upfront (est.)
body: NZ citizens get a CSP but no HECS-HELP, so the student contribution is paid each semester (about $4.8k for a science/health load at 2026 rates), plus the SSAF. Due around weeks 2–3; Semester 2 around August. [Fees calculator](https://tkluysk.github.io/higher-ed-explorer/fees.html)
